metadata.title: Stable Reference IDs Survive Viewport Chaos.
metadata.purpose: Redo of an unfinished Teardown scaffold as an hai-simple Plain-register question: why does a pixel-coordinate click break after a browser resize, and what actually survives the reflow? Lands the carry-out that a ref names the element, a coordinate only names a location.

metadata.one_flag: B02 -- the tagging pattern is real, exact implementation not pinned to one verified API in this checkout

beats.narration_text: You'd think a button's pixel position survives a resize. It doesn't — the window resizes, the pixel goes stale, and your automation misses. So what actually stays put: the pixel, or the ref?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Button at 960, 540 resize same pixel right?', hesitates on 'pixel', corrects to 'ref', lands the real question

beats.narration_text: Say your automation finds a "Confirm Order" button at pixel 960, 540 on a 1920 by 1080 page. The plan: remember that spot, click it again whenever needed. Resize the browser to 1440 by 900, and the page reflows — the button drifts to roughly 720, 405. The remembered pixel now points at empty space.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- Confirm Order button at (960,540) on a 1920x1080 page card; the page reflows to a 1440x900 card; the same pixel now sits on empty space, marked with a cross

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- remembered pixel, reflowed page
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Left card: 1920x1080 page, 'Confirm Order' button, terracotta dot at (960,540). Arrow to a second, smaller card: 1440x900, page reflowed, button visibly moved. The remembered (960,540) dot is plotted on the new card at its old relative spot -- it lands on empty space, marked with a cross. THIS EXACT BUTTON RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: The fix runs before Claude ever looks at the page. A script tags every clickable element with a stable reference id, independent of where it sits on screen. Flagged: the exact tagging method varies tool to tool — this is the general pattern, not one fixed API. Claude targets the id, not a pixel, so the tag travels with the button no matter where the layout puts it.

shot.new_visual_element: Code card: element.setAttribute('data-ref','confirm_order_1'); a terracotta FLAG marker labelled 'pattern, not one fixed API'; source credit

production_viz.label: THE ONE FLAG -- tag before Claude looks
production_viz.mechanic: A code line builds in mono on cream: element.setAttribute('data-ref', 'confirm_order_1'). Beneath it, a single terracotta FLAG marker with the caption 'pattern, not one fixed API'. Bottom-right: 'Source: Claude Quickstarts (Anthropic)'.

beats.narration_text: Watch it happen: the "Confirm Order" button sits at pixel 960, 540 on the 1920 by 1080 page, tagged with the id confirm_order_1. Resize the window to 1440 by 900 — the button reflows to roughly 720, 405. The pixel changed. The id, confirm_order_1, never did. Claude clicks the id and lands on the button either way.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- same button, same id label glued to it through the resize morph; the pixel chip changes value, the id chip does not

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- id survives, pixel doesn't
production_viz.mechanic: THE B01 BUTTON RETURNS, identical. State 1: 1920x1080 card, button at (960,540), terracotta id chip 'ref=confirm_order_1' glued to it, ink pixel chip '(960,540)' beneath. Morph to state 2: 1440x900 card, button visibly relocated, id chip UNCHANGED and still glued to the button, pixel chip now reads '(720,405)'. Final line: 'Claude clicks ref=confirm_order_1. Lands every time.'

beats.narration_text: This holds for every element tagged before Claude reads the page — resize, reflow, anything that only moves things around. It does not cover elements that appear later: a modal that opens after a click, a list that loads after scroll. Those need their own tagging pass once they exist, or Claude is aiming at nothing.

shot.new_visual_element: Split card: left, 'tagged before load' holds through resize (check); right, 'appears after load' -- untagged, struck, captioned 'needs its own pass'

production_viz.label: Both directions -- what the tag covers
production_viz.mechanic: Two panels side by side. Left, labelled 'TAGGED BEFORE LOAD': the button survives a resize arrow, checkmark. Right, labelled 'APPEARS AFTER LOAD': a modal/list element fading in with no tag, struck through in terracotta, caption 'needs its own pass'.

beats.narration_text: A pixel coordinate describes where a button was, once. A ref names the button itself — so it survives every resize the coordinate doesn't.

props.quote: A pixel coordinate describes where a button was, once. A ref names the button itself — so it survives every resize the coordinate doesn't.
props.sparkLine: A ref names it. A pixel just points.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me: assign stable refs to every clickable element on this page, so my automation survives a resize. Paste that into Claude. Does it tag elements that load in later? Does it guard against duplicate ids? Run it and see. Liam, in for Bear.
